report.summary: Chunk 4 of session.py: defines `plan()`, `_role_for()`, `_is_local_http()`, `default_participants()`, `LiveCouncilRefused`, `live_egress_seats()`, and `convene()` with live-wire gate and lane logic.
risks: plan() | medium | Duplicate class detection uses `classes.count()` which is O(n^2) per participant; could be slow for large rosters. | Add a test with many participants to measure performance.

default_participants() | medium | Lane for OllamaAdapter is derived from resolved host but comment says 'Lane derived from resolved host'; if `_is_local_http` fails to match, lane becomes 'untrusted' even for localhost. | Verify `_is_local_http` regex handles all loopback forms.

live_egress_seats() | medium | Uses `getattr(_vendors, name, None)` which returns None if module is not imported; `shipped_classes` may be empty tuple, causing all participants to be considered live if shipped_classes is empty. | Ensure `_vendors` is imported before call or handle empty case.

convene() | high | The live-wire gate checks `live` flag before checking `participants`; if `live` is False and `live_egress_seats` raises `LiveCouncilRefused`, the roster is not validated for duplicates or emptiness. | Verify that duplicate check and empty check are still performed after gate? Actually code shows they are after, but if exception is raised, checks are skipped. That is intentional per docstring.

convene() | medium | Line 'participants = tuple(participants)' is commented as 'Materialised ONCE', but the comment says 'a one-shot iterator would arrive here full, be drained by the gate, and reach sorted() empty'. However, the gate uses `participants` after converting to tuple, so no issue. Comment is explanatory.

convene() | medium | Lane override for trusted vendors sets `adapter.lane = 'trusted'` without checking if adapter already has a lane; could override a manually set lane. | Doc says 'Explicit, recorded, per-council.' but no check.
convene() | medium | The condition for remote trusted lane over HTTP checks `_is_local_http` but does not consider HTTPS endpoints. | Add test with https:// endpoint.
convene() | low | 'collided' detection uses `actors.count(a) > 1` which is O(n^2) but for small n it's fine.

handoff.purpose: Defines planning, role assignment, local host detection, default participant construction, live-wire gate, and the main convene function with safety checks.

symbols.name: plan
symbols.note: Returns a plan dict with rounds, assignments, bounds, and advisory flag; no side effects.

symbols.name: _role_for
symbols.note: Determines role from pool using index and round number.

symbols.name: _is_local_http
symbols.note: Checks if endpoint is loopback HTTP; uses regex and local host set.

symbols.name: default_participants
symbols.note: Builds default roster of CouncilAdapter instances; no I/O.

symbols.name: LiveCouncilRefused
symbols.note: RuntimeError raised when live=True not set but seats have real vendor transports.

symbols.name: live_egress_seats
symbols.note: Returns tuple of seat descriptions that could reach a real vendor; fail-closed.

symbols.name: convene
symbols.note: Main council execution function; validates participants, checks live gate, assigns lanes, returns CouncilRecord.

claims.text: Exactly what convene would do, WITHOUT calling anything. No adapter method that could reach a vendor is touched: only the identity properties (actor, independence class, lane), which are pure.
claims.why: The function only reads attributes (actor, independence_class, lane) and computes plan; no calls to adapter methods.

claims.text: True only for a loopback HTTP endpoint. localhost-ish and nothing else.
"Local" was a property of an environment variable nobody had ever set; here it is a property of the RESOLVED host, checked, not asserted.
claims.why: Reference to environment variable not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Lanes come from the council profiles, NOT from a default argument here: codex and agy are untrusted (allow-list tier ON) unless the operator opts in per council.
claims.why: Council profiles not defined in this chunk; default_participants does not set lane for anthropic/openai/google, only for local.

claims.text: The Ollama host is passed EXPLICITLY and OLLAMA_HOST is neither read for routing nor written -- normalising a remote Ollama into this process would retroactively falsify offload.py's lane="trusted" justification from a code path nobody edited.
claims.why: Reference to offload.py not in this chunk; OLLAMA_HOST environment variable not read here.

claims.text: LANE DERIVED FROM THE RESOLVED HOST, not from the provider name. OllamaAdapter defaults to lane="trusted" whatever host it is given, and "trusted" means the tier-2 allow-list is OFF and withheld is empty -- correct ONLY while no bytes leave the machine. The bench is another box on the tailnet. Passing the lane explicitly here is what keeps a REMOTE Ollama from inheriting a justification that was written for a local one.
claims.why: Code passes lane='trusted' if _is_local_http(host) else 'untrusted', overriding OllamaAdapter default.

claims.text: A seat that can reach a real vendor was offered without live=True. Deliberately NOT a ValueError: every other refusal in convene is a malformed-roster complaint, and 'you were about to spend money' must be catchable on its own.

Name every seat that could actually reach a vendor. FAIL-CLOSED. The question is not 'is this class from vendors' -- it is 'if ask() runs, does SHIPPED transport code execute'. A seat is therefore counted as LIVE unless one of these is demonstrably true: * it is not one of the shipped concrete adapters at all (the base CouncilAdapter._dispatch raises NotImplementedError, so a class defined elsewhere is the caller's own code and the caller owns it); * its _dispatch -- the transport seam -- is defined OUTSIDE daedalus.council.vendors, i.e. the test/host replaced it; * its runner / chat hook is not one of _SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS, i.e. a substitute was injected at construction. Everything else -- including an adapter shape this function has never seen -- is assumed able to spend money. If _SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS ever resolves empty (vendors renamed something), the hook test is SKIPPED rather than trivially satisfied, so the failure lands on the safe side.
claims.why: Code implements exactly those checks: isinstance against shipped_classes, dispatch module check, hook substitution check with skip if _SHIPPED_TRANSPORTS empty.

claims.text: participants are CouncilAdapter instances -- read-only, tool-less, spawned outside the repo. Every one of them is REQUESTED, and every requested participant produces exactly one chained turn per round even when it is missing: skipping an unavailable vendor would let a two-vendor council render identically to a four-vendor one.
claims.why: Behavior of missing vendors not visible in this chunk; no logic for handling missing vendors.

claims.text: trusted_vendors is the OPERATOR OPT-IN that lifts a vendor off the untrusted allow-list for this council only. It is recorded per participant, because deciding OpenAI or Google is trusted with this repo's IP is a policy decision and a default argument must not make it.
claims.why: Code sets adapter.lane = 'trusted' if adapter.vendor in trusted; trusted defaults to ().

claims.text: live is the SPEND OPT-IN and defaults to False. Any seat that still carries a shipped vendor transport (live_egress_seats) raises LiveCouncilRefused here -- before the council id, before the store, before the roster is chained, before one byte is dispatched. Offline adapters (fakes, injected runners) are unaffected, so the replay harness never has to ask for permission it does not need.
claims.why: Code checks if not live then calls live_egress_seats and raises LiveCouncilRefused before any other action (council_id, store, etc.).

claims.text: Materialised ONCE, before anything inspects it: the live-wire gate below iterates the roster, and a one-shot iterator would arrive here full, be drained by the gate, and reach sorted() empty -- a council of nobody, chained as if it were real.
claims.why: Code does participants = tuple(participants) immediately, converting iterator to tuple.

claims.text: FIRST, above every other check: a refusal that happened after the roster was chained would leave an open council on disk that nobody closed, and a refusal that happened after dispatch would not be one.
claims.why: Live check is performed before any other validation (empty, duplicate, etc.) and before any I/O.

claims.text: Two seats with one identity: local qwen2.5-coder:7b and BENCH qwen2.5-coder:7b are the same weights on two sockets and would land as one indistinguishable pair of turns. Refuse loudly rather than let the transcript claim two voices it cannot tell apart.
claims.why: Code checks for duplicate actor names and raises ValueError with descriptive message.

claims.text: Explicit, recorded, per-council. Never implied by a default.
claims.why: Code sets lane to 'trusted' only if adapter.vendor in trusted, and trusted defaults to empty frozenset.

claims.text: A trusted lane over an HTTP endpoint on ANOTHER MACHINE turns the tier-2 allow-list off and reports withheld=[] while full repo source crosses the tailnet. That is precisely the justification offload.py:193-197 rests on ("no bytes leave the machine"), borrowed by a host it was never written for. Fail closed and make
